title: Lefschetz Splitting In Bounded Triangulated Categories

items.title: Truncation functors, t-cohomology, amplitude and bounded t-structures
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ be a t-structure on a triangulated category $\mathcal T$ with translation $[1]$ ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]], [[def-triangulated-category]]), and set $\mathcal T^{\le n}:=\mathcal T^{\le0}[-n]$ and $\mathcal T^{\ge n}:=\mathcal T^{\ge0}[-n]$ for $n\in\mathbb Z$; thus $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ exactly when $X[n]\in\mathcal T^{\le0}$, and $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ exactly when $X[n]\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$.

For $X\in\mathcal T$ and $n\in\mathbb Z$, the t-structure axiom applied to the translate $X[n]$ and then shifted by $[-n]$ produces a distinguished triangle
$$\tau_{\le n}X\longrightarrow X\longrightarrow\tau_{\ge n+1}X\longrightarrow\tau_{\le n}X[1]$$
with $\tau_{\le n}X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $\tau_{\ge n+1}X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$; such a triangle is a **truncation triangle** of $X$ at $n$. Truncation triangles of the same $X$ at the same $n$ are canonically isomorphic over $X$, so the objects and maps occurring in them are determined up to unique compatible isomorphism ([[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]]); one writes $\tau_{\le n}$ and $\tau_{\ge n}$ for the resulting **truncation functors**.

The **t-cohomology** of $X$ is
$$H^n_t(X):=(\tau_{\le n}\tau_{\ge n}X)[n],$$
an object of the heart $\mathcal C=\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ ([[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]]). The **amplitude** of $X$ is the set of $n$ with $H^n_t(X)\not\cong0$; it is *contained in* an interval $[a,b]$ when $H^n_t(X)=0$ for every $n\notin[a,b]$. The t-structure is **bounded** when every object of $\mathcal T$ lies in $\mathcal T^{\le n}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$ for some integer $n$ depending on the object.

This item fixes notation and conventions only; existence, essential uniqueness and all algebraic properties of $\tau_{\le n}$, $\tau_{\ge n}$ and $H^n_t$ are proved in the two immediately following lemmas.
items.strategy: Definition pack. Apply the t-structure axiom (condition (iii) of [[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) to $X[n]$: it gives a distinguished triangle $A\to X[n]\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in\mathcal T^{\le0}$ and $B\in\mathcal T^{\ge1}$; translating by $[-n]$ and using $\mathcal T^{\le0}[-n]=\mathcal T^{\le n}$ together with $\mathcal T^{\ge1}[-n]=\mathcal T^{\ge0}[-(n+1)]=\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$ gives the displayed truncation triangle. The membership and uniqueness assertions are exactly the content of the following lemma, which also shows that a different choice of the axiom triangle changes $\tau_{\le n}X$, $\tau_{\ge n+1}X$ and the connecting map only by the unique compatible isomorphism; nothing else is proved here.

references.title: A. A. Beilinson, J. Bernstein and P. Deligne, «Faisceaux pervers», Astérisque 100 (1982), Société Mathématique de France (complete numdam PDF)

items.axiom_use: None: for a single object the t-structure axiom supplies its decomposition triangle directly, and all truncation data are unique up to unique compatible isomorphism, so no selection over a family enters any assertion.

items.title: Truncation triangles are essentially unique and give adjoint truncation functors
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ be a t-structure on a triangulated category $\mathcal T$, with truncations as in [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]].

(i) *Essential uniqueness.* For every $X$ and $n$, every distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $B\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$ is isomorphic to the truncation triangle $\tau_{\le n}X\to X\to\tau_{\ge n+1}X\to\tau_{\le n}X[1]$ by an isomorphism of triangles whose middle component is the identity of $X$; this isomorphism is unique.

(ii) *Adjunction and orthogonality.* The assignment $X\mapsto\tau_{\le n}X$ is a functor and for $T\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}(T,\tau_{\le n}X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)$, $f\mapsto(\tau_{\le n}X\to X)\circ f$, is a bijection natural in $X$; dually $\operatorname{Hom}(\tau_{\ge n}X,T)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,T)$ is a bijection for $T\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$. Moreover $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le n},\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})=0$ for every $n$.

(iii) *Aisle criteria.* $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ if and only if $\tau_{\le n}X\to X$ is an isomorphism, if and only if $\tau_{\ge n+1}X=0$, if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(X,\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})=0$; dually $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ if and only if $X\to\tau_{\ge n}X$ is an isomorphism, if and only if $\tau_{\le n-1}X=0$, if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le n-1},X)=0$.

(iv) *Extensions, direct sums and iteration.* If in a distinguished triangle two of the three vertices lie in $\mathcal T^{\le n}$ (respectively $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$), then so does the third; a finite direct sum lies in $\mathcal T^{\le n}$ (respectively $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$) if and only if each summand does. For $m\le n$ there are canonical isomorphisms $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\le n}\cong\tau_{\le m}$, $\tau_{\le n}\tau_{\le m}\cong\tau_{\le m}$, $\tau_{\ge n}\tau_{\ge m}\cong\tau_{\ge n}$ and $\tau_{\ge m}\tau_{\ge n}\cong\tau_{\ge n}$ compatible with the truncation maps, and $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\ge n}=0$ when $m<n$.
items.strategy:
Existence is the t-structure axiom; the work is uniqueness, adjunction, functoriality and the closure properties.
(1) Orthogonality for all shifts: the axiom gives $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge1})=0$, and the shift criteria of [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]] turn this into $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le n},\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})=0$ for every $n$: a map from $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ to $Y\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$ is a map $X[n]\in\mathcal T^{\le0}\to Y[n]\in\mathcal T^{\ge1}$.
(2) Uniqueness: let $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ be distinguished with $A\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$, $B\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$. For $T\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ the long exact Hom sequence of [[thm-long-exact-hom-sequences-of-a-distinguished-triangle]] gives an exact sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(T,A)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,B)$, and the last term vanishes by step (1) (also after shifting $T$), so the first map is a bijection. Applying this with $T=\tau_{\le n}X$ and with $T=A$ produces mutually inverse maps $\tau_{\le n}X\leftrightarrow A$ compatible with the maps to $X$; comparing the two triangles through the third components with [[cor-triangulated-five-lemma]] (via [[prop-distinguished-triangles-are-closed-under-shifts-and-both-rotations]]) yields the unique isomorphism of triangles over $X$. The same argument applied to two truncation triangles proves that even the truncation triangle itself is unique up to unique isomorphism over $X$.
(3) Adjunction and functoriality: the bijection in (ii) is step (2)'s sequence with $B=\tau_{\ge n+1}X$. For $f:X\to Y$ the composite $\tau_{\le n}X\to X\to Y$ factors uniquely through $\tau_{\le n}Y\to Y$ because $\tau_{\le n}Y\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$; this defines $\tau_{\le n}f$, and the uniqueness makes the assignment compatible with identities and composition. Additivity follows because for a finite biproduct the universal property identifies $\tau_{\le n}(X\oplus Y)$ with $\tau_{\le n}X\oplus\tau_{\le n}Y$; the dual statements give $\tau_{\ge n}$.
(4) Criteria (iii): if $\tau_{\ge n+1}X=0$, the truncation triangle makes $\tau_{\le n}X\to X$ an isomorphism, so $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$; conversely if $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ the triangle $X\xrightarrow{1}X\to0\to X[1]$ is a decomposition triangle, so essential uniqueness identifies its third vertex with $\tau_{\ge n+1}X=0$. For the Hom formulation, if $\operatorname{Hom}(X,\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})=0$ then the truncation map $X\to\tau_{\ge n+1}X$ is zero; the rotated triangle has zero first map, so [[prop-a-distinguished-triangle-with-zero-first-map-is-split]] makes it split and $\tau_{\ge n+1}X$, being a direct summand of $X$ whose projection is zero, vanishes; hence $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$. Conversely $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ kills $\operatorname{Hom}(X,\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})$ by the orthogonality of step (1), and the dual formulation is identical.
(5) Closures and iteration: if two vertices of a distinguished triangle lie in $\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$, the long exact $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le n},-)$ sequence and (iii) put the third there as well; the other aisle is dual, and direct sums are immediate from the orthogonality description. For $m\le n$, $\tau_{\le m}X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}\subseteq\mathcal T^{\le n}$ so (iii) identifies $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\le n}X$ and $\tau_{\le n}\tau_{\le m}X$ with $\tau_{\le m}X$; the remaining identities are dual, and for $m<n$ the composite $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\ge n}$ vanishes because $\tau_{\ge n}X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$, so $\tau_{\le n-1}\tau_{\ge n}X=0$ by (iii), and then $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\ge n}X=\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\le n-1}\tau_{\ge n}X=0$ by the iteration identities since $m\le n-1$.

references.title: A. A. Beilinson, J. Bernstein and P. Deligne, «Faisceaux pervers», Astérisque 100 (1982), Société Mathématique de France (complete numdam PDF)

items.axiom_use: None: all arguments use only the t-structure axioms, shifts, cones and long exact Hom sequences; no choice principle is invoked.

items.title: t-cohomology is functorial, additive, shift-compatible and detects amplitude
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ be a t-structure on a triangulated category $\mathcal T$, with truncations and t-cohomology as in [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]] and [[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]], and let $\mathcal C=\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ be the heart.

(i) Each $H^n_t$ is a functor from $\mathcal T$ to $\mathcal C$: for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ the induced map $H^n_t(f)$ is the unique map compatible with $f$ under the truncations, and values lie in the heart.

(ii) *Shifts.* $H^n_t(X[m])\cong H^{n+m}_t(X)$ for all $m,n\in\mathbb Z$, naturally in $X$.

(iii) *Additivity.* For a finite biproduct $X\oplus Y$ with injections $i_X,i_Y$ and projections $p_X,p_Y$, the maps $(H^n_t(i_X),H^n_t(i_Y)):H^n_t(X)\oplus H^n_t(Y)\to H^n_t(X\oplus Y)$ and $(H^n_t(p_X),H^n_t(p_Y)):H^n_t(X\oplus Y)\to H^n_t(X)\oplus H^n_t(Y)$ are mutually inverse isomorphisms; in particular $H^n_t(X\oplus Y)\cong H^n_t(X)\oplus H^n_t(Y)$ naturally.

(iv) *Amplitude detection.* If $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$ then $H^n_t(X)=0$ for every $n>m$, and if $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge m}$ then $H^n_t(X)=0$ for every $n<m$. If the t-structure is bounded ([[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]]), the converses hold: $H^n_t(X)=0$ for all $n>m$ implies $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$, and $H^n_t(X)=0$ for all $n<m$ implies $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge m}$.

(v) *Concentration and its consequences.* If $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$ then $\tau_{\ge m}X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$, and if $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge m}$ then $\tau_{\le m}X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$; if $X$ lies in both aisles then the canonical map gives $X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$. If $X$ and $Y$ both have $H^n_t=0$ for every $n\ne m$, then $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H^m_t(X),H^m_t(Y))$, $f\mapsto H^m_t(f)$, is a bijection under these canonical identifications.
items.strategy:
(i) $H^n_t$ is the composite $\tau_{\le n}\circ\tau_{\ge n}\circ[n]$ of functors from the previous lemma, so it is functorial; its values lie in the heart because $\tau_{\ge n}X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$, the truncation $\tau_{\le n}$ of an object of $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ again lies in $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ (closure under extensions in (iv) of [[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]]), and $Z\in\mathcal T^{\le n}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ is equivalent to $Z[n]\in\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ by the shift criteria of the definition.
(ii) Truncation commutes with shift: for every $a$, $\tau_{\le m}(X[a])\cong(\tau_{\le m+a}X)[a]$ and dually, because both sides satisfy the same universal property with respect to the aisle $\mathcal T^{\le m}$ (or, directly, because the shifted truncation triangle is a decomposition triangle for $X[a]$ at $m$). Hence $H^n_t(X[m])=\tau_{\le n}\tau_{\ge n}(X[m])[n]\cong\tau_{\le n+m}\tau_{\ge n+m}X[n+m]\cong H^{n+m}_t(X)$, naturally.
(iii) Additive functors preserve finite biproducts; explicitly, the injections and projections of $X\oplus Y$ satisfy the biproduct identities ([[def-biproduct]]), and applying the functorial $H^n_t$ to those identities exhibits the stated mutually inverse maps.
(iv) If $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$ and $n>m$, then $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n-1}$, hence $\tau_{\ge n}X=0$ by the aisle criterion and $H^n_t(X)=0$; the other aisle is dual. For the converses assume the t-structure is bounded, so choose $N\ge m$ with $X\in\mathcal T^{\le N}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -N}$. If $H^n_t(X)=0$ for all $n>m$, then for $k=N,N-1,\dots,m+1$ downwards: $X\in\mathcal T^{\le k}$ and the concentration identity proved in (v) below gives $\tau_{\ge k}X\cong H^k_t(X)[-k]=0$, so $X\cong\tau_{\le k-1}X\in\mathcal T^{\le k-1}$; after finitely many steps $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$. The lower bound is dual; the two arguments are independent and may be applied in either order.
(v) The identity $H^m_t(X)[-m]=\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\ge m}X$ is the definition. If $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge m}$ then $\tau_{\ge m}X\cong X$ and the first identity follows; if $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$ then $X\to\tau_{\ge m}X$ is the truncation and $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\ge m}X\cong\tau_{\ge m}X$, giving the second identity; both aisles force $X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$. For the map detection: the concentration identities provide canonical isomorphisms $X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$ and $Y\cong H^m_t(Y)[-m]$, and the composite $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H^m_t(X),H^m_t(Y))$ with those isomorphisms and the shift identification is exactly the map induced by the functor $H^m_t$, hence a bijection.

references.title: A. A. Beilinson, J. Bernstein and P. Deligne, «Faisceaux pervers», Astérisque 100 (1982), Société Mathématique de France (complete numdam PDF)

items.axiom_use: None: the argument uses finite induction on the amplitude bound, shifts and finite biproducts only; no choice principle is invoked.

items.title: Hard Lefschetz splits a bounded t-structure complex
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category with a bounded t-structure, with truncation functors and t-cohomology as in [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]] and [[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]]. Let $K\in\mathcal T$ and let $L:K\to K[2]$ be a morphism such that for every integer $j\ge0$ the map
$$H^{-j}_t(L^j):H^{-j}_t(K)\longrightarrow H^{-j}_t(K[2j])\cong H^j_t(K)$$
is an isomorphism, where the identification is the shift isomorphism $H^{j}_t(K)\cong H^{-j}_t(K[2j])$ of that lemma. Then there is an isomorphism
$$K\cong\bigoplus_j H^j_t(K)[-j]$$
in $\mathcal T$; the sum is finite because the t-structure is bounded. The isomorphism is not asserted to be canonical, and no compatibility with primitive lifts is claimed: this is the abstract splitting criterion, not the stronger primitive-compatible decomposition used in the Hodge theory of projective maps. The degenerate case in which $H^{-n}_t(K)$ and $H^n_t(K)$ are both zero (they vanish together because $H^{-n}_t(L^n)$ is an isomorphism) is covered by the same formulas, all of which are then the zero maps between zero objects.
items.strategy:
Proof by induction on the amplitude. Fix $K,L$ and use the boundedness of the t-structure to choose $n\ge0$ with $K\in\mathcal T^{\le n}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$ ([[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]]); by amplitude detection (iv) of [[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]] this is equivalent to $H^j_t(K)=0$ for $|j|>n$. We prove for every $n\ge0$ the statement: every $K\in\mathcal T^{\le n}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$ admitting such an $L$ satisfies the conclusion.
Base $n=0$: $K$ lies in the heart, so the concentration identity (v) gives $K\cong H^0_t(K)$ and the sum has the single term $j=0$.
Induction step $n\ge1$. Put $A=H^{-n}_t(K)$ and $B=H^n_t(K)$. Let $a:A[n]\to K$ be the truncation map $\tau_{\le -n}K\to K$, identified with $A[n]\to K$ by the concentration identity for $K\in\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$, and let $b:K\to B[-n]$ be the truncation map $K\to\tau_{\ge n}K$, identified with $K\to B[-n]$ by the concentration identity for $K\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$. Then $ba=0$, because $A[n]\in\mathcal T^{\le -n}$, $B[-n]\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le -n},\mathcal T^{\ge n})=0$ for $n\ge1$ ([[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]]).
Let $h=H^{-n}_t(L^n):A\to B$ be the isomorphism supplied by the hypothesis and define two morphisms by the truncated composites
$$c:=L^n[-2n]\circ a[-2n]\circ h^{-1}[-n]:B[-n]\to K,\qquad r:=h^{-1}[n]\circ b[2n]\circ L^n:K\to A[n].$$
Then $bc=1$ and $ra=1$: the first composites induce $1_B$ resp. $1_A$ on $H^n_t$ resp. $H^{-n}_t$, because $H^{-n}_t(L^n)=h$, the truncation maps $a$ and $b$ induce the canonical identifications on the extreme t-cohomology, and $H$ is functorial; since $B[-n]$ and $A[n]$ are concentrated in single degrees, map detection (v) of [[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]] promotes these cohomological identities to the displayed identities of morphisms. Put $r':=r-(rc)b$. Then $r'a=1-(rc)(ba)=1$ and $r'c=rc-(rc)(bc)=0$, while $ba=0$ and $bc=1$; hence $(r',b)\circ(a,c)$ is the identity of $A[n]\oplus B[-n]$ with respect to the biproduct structure.
Complete $(a,c):A[n]\oplus B[-n]\to K$ to a distinguished triangle and let $K_0$ be its third vertex. The left inverse $(r',b)$ makes the triangle split by [[prop-a-distinguished-triangle-splits-exactly-when-one-connecting-map-vanishes]], so $K\cong A[n]\oplus K_0\oplus B[-n]$ with $i:K_0\to K$ the remaining inclusion and $p:K\to K_0$ the remaining projection, $pi=1$.
The summands $A[n]\cong H^{-n}_t(K)[n]$ and $B[-n]$ are concentrated in the extreme degrees, so additivity (iii) of the t-cohomology lemma applied to this biproduct gives $H^{-n}_t(K)\cong A\oplus H^{-n}_t(K_0)$ and $H^n_t(K)\cong H^n_t(K_0)\oplus B$, whence $H^{\pm n}_t(K_0)=0$. Since $K_0$ is a direct summand of $K$, it lies in $\mathcal T^{\le n}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$ (closure of the aisles under direct summands, (iv) of the truncation-triangle lemma). From $K_0\in\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$ and $H^{-n}_t(K_0)=0$, the concentration identity (v) gives $\tau_{\le -n}K_0=0$, hence $K_0\in\mathcal T^{\ge -n+1}$ by the aisle criterion (iii) of the truncation-triangle lemma; dually $K_0\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $H^n_t(K_0)=0$ give $\tau_{\ge n}K_0=0$ and $K_0\in\mathcal T^{\le n-1}$.
Define $L_0:=p[2]\circ L\circ i:K_0\to K_0[2]$. For $0\le j<n$ one has $L_0^j=p[2j]L^ji$, so by functoriality $H^{-j}_t(L_0^j)=H^{-j}_t(p[2j])\circ H^{-j}_t(L^j)\circ H^{-j}_t(i)$. The outer maps are isomorphisms: $H^{-j}_t(i)$ is an isomorphism because $H^{-j}_t(K)\cong H^{-j}_t(K_0)$ for $-n<j<n$ by additivity and the concentration of $A[n]$ and $B[-n]$, and $H^{-j}_t(p[2j])$ has the inverse $H^{-j}_t(i[2j])$ because $pi=1$. Hence $H^{-j}_t(L_0^j)$ is an isomorphism whenever $H^{-j}_t(L^j)$ is; for $j\ge n$ both sides vanish. Thus $L_0$ satisfies the hard Lefschetz hypothesis on $K_0\in\mathcal T^{\le n-1}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -(n-1)}$ and the induction hypothesis decomposes $K_0$. Combining with $K\cong A[n]\oplus K_0\oplus B[-n]$, $A[n]=H^{-n}_t(K)[n]$ and $B[-n]=H^n_t(K)[-n]$ gives the asserted finite direct sum for $K$.

items.title: Graded hard Lefschetz has a canonical primitive decomposition
items.statement:
Let $H^j$ be objects of an abelian category, zero for all but finitely many integers $j$, and let $L:H^j\to H^{j+2}$ be morphisms whose iterates give isomorphisms $L^r:H^{-r}\to H^r$ for every $r\ge0$. Put $P^{-r}:=\ker\bigl(L^{r+1}:H^{-r}\to H^{r+2}\bigr)$ for $r\ge0$, and $P^{-r}=0$ for $r<0$. Then for every $r\ge0$ the powers of $L$ induce finite direct sum decompositions
$$H^{-r}=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}L^jP^{-r-2j},\qquad H^{r}=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}L^{r+j}P^{-r-2j},$$
each displayed power $L^j$ or $L^{r+j}$ restricts to a monomorphism on its primitive source, and both decompositions are natural for morphisms commuting with $L$. This is a decomposition statement for graded objects in an abelian category; it does not identify primitive objects with classes annihilated by an untruncated map on a derived splitting of a complex.
items.strategy: Fix $r\ge0$. The restriction of $L^{r+1}:H^{-r}\to H^{r+2}$ to $\operatorname{im}(L:H^{-r-2}\to H^{-r})$ is the composite $L^{r+2}=L^{r+1}L$, which is an isomorphism by hypothesis; hence the kernel of $L^{r+1}$ meets $\operatorname{im}L$ trivially and $L^{r+1}$ is an epimorphism, with the explicit right inverse $s=L\circ(L^{r+2})^{-1}:H^{r+2}\to H^{-r}$ (here $(L^{r+2})^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of the isomorphism). The sequence $0\to P^{-r}\to H^{-r}\xrightarrow{L^{r+1}}H^{r+2}\to0$ is therefore short exact ([[def-exact-sequence-and-short-exact-sequence-in-an-abelian-category]]), and the splitting lemma ([[thm-splitting-lemma-in-an-abelian-category]], [[def-split-short-exact-sequence-in-an-abelian-category]]) gives a biproduct decomposition $H^{-r}\cong P^{-r}\oplus H^{r+2}$ whose second inclusion is $s$. Since $L^{r+2}=L^{r+1}L$ is an isomorphism, the map $L$ on $H^{-r-2}$ is a split monomorphism, and its image equals $\operatorname{im}s$: indeed $s=L(L^{r+2})^{-1}$ lands in $\operatorname{im}L$, and $Ly=s(L^{r+2}y)$, so every element of $\operatorname{im}L$ is in $\operatorname{im}s$. Hence $H^{-r}=P^{-r}\oplus LH^{-r-2}$ with explicit projection the idempotent $L(L^{r+2})^{-1}L^{r+1}$ ([[def-image-and-coimage-in-a-category-with-kernels-and-cokernels]] for kernels and images). Iterating this decomposition through $H^{-r-2},H^{-r-4},\dots$ terminates because the graded family is finite: since $L$ is a monomorphism on each $H^{-m}$ with $m\ge1$, it carries the direct sum $H^{-r-2}=P^{-r-2}\oplus LH^{-r-4}$ to the direct sum $LH^{-r-2}=LP^{-r-2}\oplus L^2H^{-r-4}$, and continuing gives $H^{-r}=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}L^jP^{-r-2j}$. Each displayed power restricts to a composite of the split monomorphisms $L$ on the intermediate $H^{-m}$, $m\ge1$, hence is a monomorphism on its primitive source. Applying the isomorphism $L^r:H^{-r}\to H^r$ to the first decomposition and using $L^rL^j=L^{r+j}$ gives the second. Naturality: a morphism of graded objects commuting with $L$ commutes with the isomorphisms $L^{r+2}$ and their inverses, with the kernels $P^{-r}$, with the explicit projections and injections, and hence with the whole finite construction; the same argument applies at each induction step. Degenerate cases (a zero $H^{-r}$, or a finite family ending before the induction does) are covered by the same split maps.

items.title: The nilpotent Lefschetz filtration is canonical and self-dual
items.statement:
Let $N$ be a nilpotent endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space $H$ over a field. There is a unique increasing finite filtration $W$ of $H$ such that $NW_i\subset W_{i-2}$ for all $i$ and $N^r:\operatorname{Gr}^W_rH\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-r}H$ is an isomorphism for every $r\ge0$. It is given intrinsically by
$$W_i=\sum_{a,b\ge0,\ a-b=i}\ker N^{a+1}\cap\operatorname{im}N^b.$$
If in addition $S$ is a nondegenerate bilinear form on $H$ with $S(Nv,w)+S(v,Nw)=0$ for all $v,w$, then $(W_i)^\perp=W_{-i-1}$ for every $i$, and consequently $S$ induces a perfect pairing between $\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-i}H$; moreover for $i\ge0$ the form $S_i([v],[w]):=S(v,N^iw)$ on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH$ is well defined and nondegenerate.
items.strategy:
Existence and the intrinsic formula. Use a Jordan-string basis of $N$ ([[thm-nilpotent-jordan-string-basis]]): in a chain $v_0,\dots,v_{l-1}$ with $Nv_t=v_{t-1}$, $Nv_0=0$, assign $v_t$ the weight $2t-l+1$. The resulting filtration satisfies $NW_i\subset W_{i-2}$ and pairs the graded pieces symmetrically; on each chain, $\ker N^{a+1}\cap\operatorname{im}N^b$ is the span of the $v_t$ with $t\le\min(a,l-1-b)$, and under $a-b=i$ the largest such index is $\lfloor(i+l-1)/2\rfloor$, with negative values giving $0$ and values beyond $l-1$ giving the whole chain. Kernels and images decompose chainwise, so the intrinsic formula holds for this filtration, independently of the chosen Jordan basis.
Uniqueness and hard Lefschetz. For a filtration satisfying the two conditions, apply the graded hard Lefschetz lemma ([[lem-graded-hard-lefschetz-has-a-canonical-primitive-decomposition]]) with degrees reversed to the graded maps $N:\operatorname{Gr}^W_t\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{t-2}$: this gives, for every $q\ge0$ and $t\le -q$, the surjectivity of $N^q:\operatorname{Gr}^W_{t+2q}\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_t$ used below (composite of an isomorphism with its inverse factor). Choose a basis of each primitive graded piece of weight $r\ge0$, lift a primitive class to $v\in W_r$; its primitivity makes $N^{r+1}v\in W_{-r-3}$. The surjectivity just recorded, iterated downward through the finite filtration, produces $u\in W_{r-1}$ with $N^{r+1}u=N^{r+1}v$: correct the error successively at decreasing weights, which terminates because $W_i=0$ for $i\ll0$. Replace $v$ by $v-u$, so that $N^{r+1}v=0$ while the primitive graded class is unchanged. The strings $v,Nv,\dots,N^rv$ obtained from all primitive graded basis classes have independent associated graded classes, hence form a basis of $H$ by dimension count. Since each $N^iv$ lies in $W_{r-2i}$ with nonzero graded class, the span of those basis vectors of $W$-weight at most $i$ is exactly $W_i$; computing that span chainwise as in the first paragraph shows that the given $W$ equals the intrinsic formula $W_i=\sum_{a-b=i}\ker N^{a+1}\cap\operatorname{im}N^b$. That formula depends only on $N$, so $W$ is unique.
Self-duality. Assume $S(Nv,w)+S(v,Nw)=0$ and put $W'_i:=(W_{-i-1})^\perp$. The skew-adjointness gives $NW'_i\subset W'_{i-2}$: test $Nv$ against $w\in W_{-i+1}$, for which $Nw\in W_{-i-1}$. The associated graded objects of $W'$ are the duals of those of $W$ in opposite degrees, and the induced maps $N^r$ on them are, up to the sign $(-1)^r$, the transposes of the hard Lefschetz isomorphisms for $W$; hence $W'$ satisfies the same two defining conditions. Uniqueness forces $W'=W$, i.e. $(W_i)^\perp=W_{-i-1}$. (The orthogonal complement is computed with respect to a nondegenerate bilinear form: $B^\flat$ is an isomorphism and $U^\perp=(B^\flat)^{-1}(\operatorname{ann}U)$ as in [[thm-bilinear-forms-correspond-to-linear-maps-into-the-dual]], [[def-annihilators-under-the-evaluation-pairing]] and [[thm-double-annihilator-and-annihilator-dimension]], so that $U^{\perp\perp}=U$ and $\dim U+\dim U^\perp=\dim H$ by [[thm-rank-nullity]], [[thm-dimension-of-a-linear-subspace]] and [[cor-dimension-of-a-direct-sum]].)
Descent of the form. The self-duality identity makes $S$ descend to a perfect pairing between opposite graded pieces (their radicals are exactly the lower filtration terms). Composing with the isomorphism $N^i:\operatorname{Gr}^W_i\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-i}$ for $i\ge0$ yields the form $S_i([v],[w])=S(v,N^iw)$ on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH$: independence of representatives holds because an error in $W_{i-1}$ is orthogonal to $W_{-i}$, and $N^i$ carries an error in $W_{i-1}$ into $W_{-i-1}$, orthogonal to $W_i$; nondegeneracy follows because $N^ia$ orthogonal to $W_i$ implies $a$ orthogonal to $N^iW_i$, i.e. $N^ia\in(W_i)^\perp=W_{-i-1}$, which forces $a\in W_{i-1}$ by injectivity of $N^i$ on the graded piece.

title: Lefschetz Splitting In Bounded Triangulated Categories Examples

items.title: Hard Lefschetz splitting for a three-degree complex
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal T=D^b(\mathbf{vect}^{fd}_k)$ be the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces with its canonical t-structure. Take
$$K=k[2]\oplus k\oplus k[-2]\in\mathcal T,$$
and let $L:K\to K[2]$ identify the first summand $k[2]$ with the shifted second summand $k[2]$ of $K[2]$, the second summand $k$ with the shifted third summand $k$ of $K[2]$, and the third summand $k[-2]$ with $0$. Its nonzero t-cohomology objects are
$$H^{-2}_t(K)=k,\qquad H^0_t(K)=k,\qquad H^2_t(K)=k,$$
and for every $j\ge0$ the map $H^{-j}_t(L^j)$ is an isomorphism: $j=0$ and $j=2$ are the two Lefschetz steps, while for $j=1$ and for $j\ge3$ both sides are zero. Consequently the splitting of [[lem-hard-lefschetz-splits-a-bounded-t-structure-complex]] returns exactly
$$K\cong H^{-2}_t(K)[2]\oplus H^0_t(K)\oplus H^2_t(K)[-2]=k[2]\oplus k\oplus k[-2].$$
This example tests the abstract splitting on the simplest complex with two hard Lefschetz steps; it does not test primitive-lift compatibility.
items.strategy: The finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces form a full abelian subcategory of the category of $k$-modules, closed under kernels, cokernels and finite direct sums ([[thm-modules-over-a-ring-form-an-abelian-category]], [[thm-rank-nullity]], [[thm-first-isomorphism-theorem-in-an-abelian-category]], [[cor-dimension-of-a-direct-sum]]); it is essentially small, so the derived-category construction of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]] applies and $\mathcal T$ is triangulated ([[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]]) with the canonical bounded t-structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]], [[thm-the-canonical-pair-is-a-t-structure]]). In this t-structure the truncation triangles are supplied by the canonical truncations of complexes ([[lem-canonical-truncation-is-a-complex-and-has-the-claimed-cohomology]], [[thm-canonical-truncations-fit-a-distinguished-triangle]]), so by the essential uniqueness and amplitude detection of [[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]] and [[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]] the abstract $H^j_t$ of a bounded complex is its usual $j$-th cohomology object. The displayed $K$ is a finite direct sum of shifts of $k$, so $H^{-2}_t(K)=H^0_t(K)=H^2_t(K)=k$ by the shift rule of the t-cohomology lemma, and all other $H^j_t(K)$ vanish. On the first summand $L$ is the canonical isomorphism $k[2]\cong k[2]$, on the second the canonical isomorphism $k\cong k$; hence $H^{-2}_t(L)$ is the identity of $k$, $H^0_t(L)$ the identity of $k$, and $H^{-2}_t(L^2)$ and the higher iterates pair the first with the third summand and vanish afterwards, again isomorphisms; the remaining maps $H^{-j}_t(L^j)$ involve a zero source or target. The hard Lefschetz hypothesis of the splitting lemma is therefore satisfied, with amplitude in $[-2,2]$, and the lemma's conclusion is the displayed finite direct sum; both extreme terms are $k[2]$ and $k[-2]$ and the middle term is $k$.
